confirmed: Source identity and version are correct: arXiv:2506.12879v1 [cs.HC], 15 Jun 2025, 26 PDF pages, with the DIS 2025 header; the title and author list match (PDF p. 1; Appendix A, pp. 21-26). The complete markdown, including references and appendices, was read.

The original study is a formative between-subjects Wizard-of-Oz comparison. Random assignment is not reported, so no randomized people study can be confirmed and n_randomized must remain null (PDF pp. 6-8, Sections 5-5.4; pp. 21-26, appendices).

Retain design_class = other and context_class = none: all groups used the same Fusion360 Generative Design tool, while the comparison varied human-operated support. This is neither an AI-versus-human output comparison nor a synthesis, and no randomized AI-assistance contrast is documented (PDF pp. 6-8, Sections 4.3-5.4).

Twenty designers were recruited and analyzed, with five in each of SocratAIs, HephAIstus, Expert-Freeform, and No Support; all completed the task. These are people, not candidate designs or ratings, and the analyzed sample is below 50 (PDF p. 7, Section 5.1; p. 9, Section 6; p. 10, Table 2 and Figure 3; p. 21, Table 4).

The support operators are separate from the analyzed designers: the first author enacted SocratAIs and HephAIstus, and four external Autodesk experts enacted Expert-Freeform (PDF p. 7, Section 5.4.1; p. 17, Section 7.3; p. 21, Table 5).

The solver generated around 20 candidate designs; each designer selected three feasible parts, and the researchers used the highest-scoring part as that designer’s final design. These design counts do not increase the participant count (PDF p. 9, Section 5.5.1).

The reported string and one-line finding reproduce the printed feasibility statistics: supported M = 3.5, SD = 1.4; No Support M = 1.0, SD = 0.0. The supported n = 15 is the three groups of five documented in Table 2, versus five unsupported designers (PDF p. 9, Section 6.1.1; p. 10, Table 2 and Figure 3).

All recorded group means are correct: SocratAIs 4.0, HephAIstus 3.2, Expert-Freeform 3.4, and No Support 1, with n = 5 per group. The outcome-score row was recovered directly with PyMuPDF find_tables and agrees with Figure 3 (PDF p. 10, Table 2 and Figure 3).

No inferential test of the design-feasibility difference is reported; the authors explicitly caution against conclusions about statistically significant differences between support conditions (PDF p. 10, continuation of Section 6.1.1). The statistical tests mentioned in footnote 10 concern population characteristics, not design outcomes (PDF p. 15, Section 7.1).

The output rubric awards one point each for structural analysis, load setup, optimized mass, fastener clearance, and bounding dimensions. The analysis uses one final design score per participant; no novelty or across-person diversity score is reported (PDF p. 9, Section 5.5.1; p. 10, Table 2).

The demographic and compensation numbers are printed as recorded: ages 20-42, M = 26.1, SD = 5.9; at least two years of CAD/Fusion360 experience; 20 USD per hour. Recruitment is from North American universities and Upwork, without a complete participant-country statement (PDF p. 7, Section 5.1).

The recorded task timings match the text: 30-minute onboarding, up to 70 minutes for Part 1, a 30-minute solver break, up to 30 minutes for Part 2, and observed work durations of 31-99 minutes (PDF p. 7, Sections 5 and 5.3).

The supplementary example video is explicitly mentioned and is separate from the PDF appendix (PDF p. 9, Section 5.5.2). This is an original empirical paper, so synthesis counts and pooled meta-analytic estimates are not applicable (PDF pp. 6-10, Sections 5-6.1).
The core = no decision and criterion_2_at_least_50_people = not_met remain correct despite correcting the output criterion (PDF p. 7, Section 5.1; p. 10, Table 2 and Figure 3).
summary: The PDF confirms 20 analyzed designers and the reported feasibility statistics, but documents no randomized assignment to generative-AI assistance. Correct the outcome eligibility, human-support comparison, Autodesk involvement, appendix description, and five unfinished coding fields; core exclusion remains justified.
